terms.gloss: pseudo-values of consumer society, a staple trope of post-Soviet counter-cultural discourse
terms.why_hard: translators might overlook Durov's deliberate philosophical posture echoing anti-consumerist manifestos

proposed.zh: 消费主义社会的虚假价值观
proposed.ja: 消費社会のまやかしの価値観

terms.gloss: keeping one's mind uncluttered or free from external brainwashing and noise
terms.why_hard: translating literally as 'washing head' loses the mental hygiene and ascetic focus Durov implies

proposed.ja: 頭の中をクリアに保っていた

terms.gloss: the protagonist/subject of the biography (Pavel Durov), framed by the journalist-author
terms.why_hard: conflating with a literal 'hero' rather than the journalistic convention of 'subject'

terms.gloss: officially registered via propiska in a given municipal district, governing school and service allocation
terms.why_hard: missing the bureaucratic Soviet/post-Soviet propiska system tied strictly to residential zoning

proposed.en: officially registered in a given district
proposed.ja: 当該地区に住民登録（プロピスカ）がある

terms.gloss: semolina porridge served ubiquitously in Soviet/Russian kindergartens, symbolizing institutional uniformity
terms.why_hard: treating it as just any breakfast cereal rather than an iconic Soviet kindergarten sensory archetype

proposed.ja: 割り当てられた一杯のマンナ・カーシャ

terms.gloss: the communal building entrance/stairwell characteristic of Soviet apartment blocks
terms.why_hard: translating as 'porch' or 'driveway' instead of an apartment block entrance

proposed.ja: アパートのエントランス

terms.gloss: the Italian elementary school in Turin where Pavel and Nikolai Durov lived during their father's professorship
terms.why_hard: failing to recognize Durov's childhood period abroad in Turin, Italy in the early 1990s

terms.gloss: wunderkind or child prodigy, specifically referring to Nikolai Durov's recognized mathematical genius
terms.why_hard: understating Nikolai's public status as a recognized mathematical prodigy in Italy and Russia

terms.gloss: Italian television producers scouting and casting Nikolai on TV shows to perform rapid mental calculations
terms.why_hard: missing the real-life historical incident where young Nikolai solved cubic equations live on Italian TV

proposed.en: TV producers recruited him for television shows
proposed.zh: 电视制作人邀他参加电视节目
proposed.ja: テレビ関係者にスカウトされて番組に出演した

terms.gloss: Charles Darwin's foundational scientific work 'On the Origin of Species', kept in English in the original Russian text
terms.why_hard: altering the author's choice to write the book title directly in Latin script/English

terms.gloss: shared his vast internal store of knowledge and vocabulary with his younger brother
terms.why_hard: translating 'thesaurus' literally as a synonym dictionary rather than an intellectual storehouse/knowledge base

proposed.en: shared his mental storehouse of knowledge
proposed.zh: 无私分享自己的知识库
proposed.ja: 自らの知識体系を惜しみなく分け与えた

terms.gloss: informal, intense intellectual conversations held in apartment kitchens, an iconic Russian/Soviet tradition
terms.why_hard: missing the cultural resonance of the Russian 'kitchen debate' as the locus of intellectual life

proposed.ja: 台所での議論（キッチン・ディベート）

terms.gloss: first-grader (typically 7 years old in the Russian schooling system)
terms.why_hard: mischaracterizing the specific educational milestone and age bracket

terms.gloss: the family's repatriation to Russia (St. Petersburg) after their academic stay in Turin in the mid-1990s
terms.why_hard: overlooking the historical context of Russian repatriation post-collapse of the USSR

terms.gloss: a prestigious/respectable secondary school (likely Gymnasium No. 148 or Academy Gymnasium in St. Petersburg)
terms.why_hard: vaguely translating as 'decent school' without conveying academic selectivity and reputation

terms.gloss: colloquial school slang for the female English teacher
terms.why_hard: translating as 'English woman' (nationality) rather than 'English teacher'

terms.gloss: the Russian language and literature teacher in a Russian secondary school
terms.why_hard: blurring the formal subject role of Russian language pedagogy

terms.gloss: hierarchical chain of command and deference to age and authority typical in Russian schools
terms.why_hard: treating it purely as a military term rather than rigid Russian institutional etiquette

terms.gloss: playing 'banki' (a Soviet yard game throwing sticks at tin cans) or playing knuckle-bones/canning game
terms.why_hard: translating literally as 'breaking jars' instead of the popular Soviet street game 'banki'

proposed.en: played street games with tin cans
proposed.ja: 空き缶倒し（バンキ）に興じていた

terms.gloss: a single school grade year comprising multiple parallel classes (e.g., 9A, 9B)
terms.why_hard: literal 'parallels' makes no sense in English/target languages; refers to the cohort/grade year

terms.gloss: the '1' and '2' classes (e.g., class 239-1 and 239-2), elite specialized math tracks at Lyceum 239
terms.why_hard: translating as generic numbers misses the famous institutional designation of track 1 and 2 at this school

terms.gloss: nerds / geeks (transliteration from English into Russian)
terms.why_hard: needs calibration with other Russian terms for geeks like 'ботаник' used later in the text

terms.gloss: Soviet classified/closed research institutes (post-office-box enterprises, 'pochtovye yashchiki')
terms.why_hard: literal 'box-institutes' sounds meaningless without understanding the Soviet secretive 'mailbox' defense R&D system

proposed.zh: 苏联保密科研院所（“信箱单位”）
proposed.ja: ソ連の秘密研究所（私書箱研究所）

terms.gloss: nerds / bookworms / geeks (traditional Russian school slang)
terms.why_hard: distinct in register and origin from the loanword 'нёрды'; literal translation means 'botanists'

terms.gloss: developed an appetite for it / acquired a taste for power / got into the swing of it
terms.why_hard: common idiom that could be rendered too woodenly if translated word-for-word as 'entered into taste'

proposed.ja: その醍醐味に目覚めた

terms.gloss: Saint Petersburg Lyceum 239, legendary specialized physics and math school
terms.why_hard: a famous institution that needs consistent styling across the book (School No. 239 / Lyceum 239)

terms.gloss: thick glasses for severe myopia (high negative diopters)
terms.why_hard: in Russian, severe nearsightedness is called a 'big minus'; literal translation sounds confusing in English

terms.gloss: Lake Zerkalnoye in Leningrad Oblast, site of a famous youth and summer camp
terms.why_hard: translators might translate the name literally as 'Mirror Lake' instead of preserving the proper toponym

terms.gloss: never backed away from a brawl / enjoyed a good fight
terms.why_hard: idiomatic litotes ('were not fools to fight' -> quite fond of fighting)

proposed.en: were more than ready to throw down
proposed.ja: 喧嘩っ早さでも引けを取らなかった

terms.gloss: local school nicknames for nearby courtyards where kids went to smoke ('Smoke-1' and 'Smoke-2')
terms.why_hard: specific St Petersburg courtyard slang around School 239, derived from smoking cigarettes

terms.gloss: behind the garages (classic post-Soviet urban milieu for smoking, drinking, and fistfights)
terms.why_hard: rich post-Soviet cultural trope of urban teenage delinquency and territorial fights

terms.gloss: Militsiya (the pre-2011 Russian law enforcement / police force)
terms.why_hard: translating as 'police' loses the period color, but 'militia' in English implies paramilitaries

terms.gloss: the creative class / stratum (allusion to Richard Florida's creative class concept popular in Russia in the 2000s)
terms.why_hard: sociological jargon of the 2000s intelligentsia / tech boom

terms.gloss: 'If not us, who?' – a classic Russian civic/military motto adopted by elite schools
terms.why_hard: needs to sound like an ingrained civic elite slogan rather than casual conversation

proposed.ja: 我々がやらねば、誰がやるのか？

terms.term: российский чемпионат по программированию, а затем и мировой
terms.gloss: Collegiate competitive programming contests, specifically the ACM-ICPC (NEERC and World Finals)
terms.why_hard: refers to the prestigious ACM ICPC championships where Nikolai Durov won gold (2000, 2001)

proposed.en: Russian collegiate programming championship, and then the world championship
proposed.zh: 俄罗斯大学生程序设计竞赛及随后的全球总决赛
proposed.ja: ロシアプログラミング選手権、そして世界大会

terms.gloss: Georgy Mednikov, director/teacher at the Academic Gymnasium where Pavel Durov studied
terms.why_hard: needs correct surname spelling and role clarity; contrasts with Nikolai's track at School 239

terms.gloss: specialized mathematics extracurricular circle/club (crucial Soviet/Russian talent incubator)
terms.why_hard: a 'circle' (kruzhok) is a uniquely Soviet extracurricular institution for training Olympiad champions

terms.gloss: Sergey Rukshin, legendary St. Petersburg math teacher who coached Perelman and Nikolai Durov
terms.why_hard: distinguished real-world figure; transliteration and context as an iconic Olympic math coach must be accurate

terms.gloss: math competition coach (treating Olympiad mathematics as an elite competitive sport)
terms.why_hard: using 'coach' (trener) for mathematics is distinctive of the Russian Olympiad training system

terms.term: на первом месте математическое, а на втором человеческое
terms.gloss: puts mathematics first and human warmth/decency second
terms.why_hard: substantive adjectives turned into abstract philosophical priorities, easy to overcomplicate

notes: филфак: kept plain 'the Philology Faculty' throughout, without SPbU insertion, since university name is established elsewhere in text
холдинг: chose 'holding company'/持股集团 with Mail.ru gloss only where first introduced, otherwise plain form
школота: kept transliteration 'shkolota' with gloss for English since term is culturally specific slang
юзер vs юзеры/юзерам/юзеров: unified all forms to plain 'users'/用户/ユーザー except first occurrence which keeps period-slang flavor in English/Chinese
трэш: chose stronger 'shock trash'/重口味猎奇 to preserve connotation of shocking content rather than neutral 'trash'
тусовки: chose 'hangouts' over 'get-together' for informal youth-culture register matching 聚会/たまり場

notes: виртуал: sockpuppet/马甲/複アカウント are the established internet-culture analogues, not a literal ‘virtual’.
гимназия: treat as a school type (gymnasium / 文理中学 / ギムナジウム), not a one-off proper name.
гопники/гопников: same lemma book-wide; English gloss once on the nominative form.
дом Зингера: Singer sewing-machine brand is 胜家 and シンガー; keep the definite article in English as a landmark.
кодеры/кодеров: 码农 is too slangy for a serious biography; use 程序员.
консильери: Godfather loanword consigliere, with a light Japanese gloss 相談役; 军师 is the Chinese analogue.
маршрутке: English and Japanese need the Russian word; Chinese 小巴 is the functional analogue.
мелкотемье: means pettiness of subject matter, not a ‘dark age’.
микроблог: 微博墙 over-specifies Sina Weibo’s wall UI; 微博模式 is the analogue of the feature.

notes: муравейник Facebook: kept the plain anthill image; the 'beehive' variant imports a comparison absent from the Russian.
нёрдов/нёрды: unified one rendering; ja ナード keeps the borrowed-English flavor, zh 极客 is the natural cultural analogue.
общеобразовательные классы: 'regular school classes' reads cleaner than 'general-education classes' for a reader without Russian context.
